orientation.title: Kerala, Palakkad and the healing village
orientation.p1: Kerala is a state on the south-west coast of India. Palakkad is an inland district, set in a gap in the Western Ghats, and is farming country: paddy, coconut and forest rather than beach.
orientation.p2: Kairali — The Ayurvedic Healing Village stands at Kodumbu, outside Palakkad town. Patients stay in individual brick villas among lawns, palms and a water channel. Treatment blocks, consulting rooms, pharmacy and kitchen are on the same site.
orientation.p3: The village is run by the Kairali Ayurvedic Group — in Ayurveda since 1908, five generations of physicians — and is accredited by NABH, India's National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers.
orientation.getting_here: Palakkad railway station 25 km · Coimbatore airport approximately 66 km by road · Cochin airport approximately 114 km by road or Calicut airport approximately 116 km by road. Transfer prices are on page {page}.
orientation.a1: Ayurveda is a traditional system of medicine originating in India. It reads illness as a loss of balance, and treats it in two movements: first clearing what has accumulated, then rebuilding strength.
orientation.a2: A physician examines the patient, establishes their constitution, and prescribes a protocol for that individual. Therapies use warm medicated oils, herbal preparations and steam, and the prescription is reviewed daily.
orientation.a3: This is why a stay has a minimum duration. The clearing stage cannot safely be shortened, and the rebuilding stage consolidates the treatment: three nights for a preventive assessment, seven for most restorative programmes, fourteen for Panchakarma and chronic conditions, twenty-one where recovery is the aim.
orientation.grounds_alt: Water channel running between patient cottages and lawns at the healing village
orientation.callout: Ayurveda at Kairali is practised as medicine, under physicians, with daily review. It is not a spa treatment and it is not presented as a cure. Programmes are named for the conditions they address, and outcomes are discussed in consultation.

accommodation.title: Accommodation categories
accommodation.intro: Kairali — The Ayurvedic Healing Village is an NABH-accredited hospital. A patient is admitted to a treatment programme and accommodated in a villa for its duration; the tariff is a single per-night inpatient rate that covers the villa, the prescribed diet, the prescribed therapies and daily physician consultation, with GST included. The villa category changes the accommodation; it does not change the medical programme. Four categories are published.

accommodation.closing: The tariff on {pages} gives each group's per-night rate for all four categories, so a patient chooses the programme first and the villa second. Every villa is on the hospital grounds, within walking distance of the treatment blocks and consulting rooms.

opd.title: Outpatient & Day Treatment Rates
opd.standfirst: Single Ayurvedic treatments, consultations and classes for patients attending by the day, without admission. Every treatment is given under the supervision of an Ayurvedic physician (BAMS, India).
opd.cover_alt: Herbal poultices and brass vessels of medicated oil prepared for treatment
opd.how_p1: Kairali — The Ayurvedic Healing Village is an NABH-accredited Ayurvedic hospital at Kodumbu, Palakkad. Patients who live nearby, or who are staying elsewhere, may attend for single treatments by the day rather than being admitted to a residential programme.
opd.how_p2: Every course of day treatment begins with an outpatient consultation. An Ayurvedic physician (BAMS, India) examines the patient and writes a treatment plan; the treatments on the following pages are then given by trained therapists as that plan prescribes. Treatments are not booked directly from the list without a consultation.
opd.how_p3: The durations shown are the published treatment times.

opd.gst_text: Under Government of India GST regulations, Ayurvedic treatment services administered by an NABH-accredited hospital as part of a plan prescribed by an Ayurvedic physician registered in India are exempt from GST. The rates in this list are therefore GST-exempt when taken as part of such a plan. Treatments taken without a consultation or prescribed plan may attract GST at the prevailing rate, currently 18%.
